chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Husayn Al-Qalanisi, or one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The servant may make an exception in his oath for a period between it and forty days, if he forgets.

key_terms.يَسْتَثْنِيَ: To make an exception / stipulate a condition

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making an exception in an oath if one forgets to state it immediately?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic mechanism of 'istithna' (exception) in oaths, granting the swearer a grace period of up to forty days to rectify an omission due to forgetfulness. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease (yusr) and the preservation of the oath's validity while allowing for practical flexibility in daily commitments.
